issues.legal_issue: An insolvency court may determine title to property transferred beyond the statutory period when the transfer is alleged to have been sham or fictitious and void from its inception.
material_facts: The insolvent had executed a deed of gift in favour of his wife about seven years before insolvency proceedings began.
The receiver applied to the insolvency court to have the deed declared void and inoperative, alleging it was a sham transaction.
The insolvency court held the deed void and inoperative; the High Court reversed, ruling that the court could not examine a transfer made beyond the two-year period.
issues.conclusion: The two-year limitation applies to transfers that are voidable, not to a transfer alleged to be nominal, sham or fictitious and void from the outset. The insolvency court had jurisdiction under section 4 to determine the transfer’s validity and title; the appeal was allowed and the matter remitted to the High Court for disposal on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920 gives the insolvency court broad power to determine questions of title, subject to the Act’s other provisions. Section 53 concerns voidable transfers and its two-year period does not restrict the court’s jurisdiction over a transfer that is a nullity because it was nominal, sham or fictitious and passed no title. The Court relied on Haji Anwar Khan v. Mohammad Khan; Madan Kumar v. M/s. Hari Narain Agrawal; Padamsi Premchand v. Laxman Vishnu Deshpande; Radha Krishna Thakur v. Official Receiver; Biseswar Chaudhuri v. Kanhai Singh; G. N. Godbole v. Mt. Nani Bai; and Budha Mal v. Official Receiver, and overruled Amjad Ali v. Nand Lal Tandon.

predicates.insolvency_proceeding: The dispute arises in a proceeding to administer the property of a person adjudged insolvent.
predicates.transfer_challenged_as_sham_or_fictitiou: A receiver or other party challenges a purported transfer on the ground that it was nominal, sham or fictitious from its inception.
predicates.transfer_outside_voidable_challenge_peri: The purported transfer was made outside the period in which a voidable transfer may be challenged in the insolvency proceeding.

issues.definition: When an insolvency proceeding concerns a purported transfer challenged as sham or fictitious and made outside the period for challenging voidable transfers, the insolvency court may determine title to the property.
